title: The Quietest Beach Towns in Florida (2026)
dek: Ten Florida beach towns where the nights are dark and the beach is the main event, from a $375K Gulf town to island hideaways, with the trade off that comes with each.
body:
The quietest beach towns in Florida are Port St. Joe, Crescent Beach and Navarre Beach. Each has a great beach, almost no nightlife and no big resort strip, and Port St. Joe's typical home price of about $425K makes it the most reachable of the three.

Of the 167 towns we score, 18 combine our lowest nightlife score with a strong beach. We picked ten of them across every part of the coast and a wide range of prices. Quiet usually comes with a cost, so each one has its catch.

Beach scores are out of 5. Prices are the typical figures on our town pages. *Melbourne Beach is the state's 2024 estimate. Resident counts are year round people only, so island towns like Captiva, Navarre Beach and Longboat Key fill up with visitors in season even though very few people live there full time.

That is the honest catch with quiet: the smallest places on this list are small because most homes are second homes and rentals. Off season they are as quiet as anywhere in Florida. In March or July, expect more people on the beach than the resident count suggests. Englewood is the opposite case, a real town of about 20,800 people that stays quiet because there is little nightlife, not because nobody lives there.

Port St. Joe

A small town on St. Joseph Bay with calm, clear water, bay sunsets and the beaches of Cape San Blas a short drive out. You will hear boats and birds, not bars. The catch: the nearest big airport is in Panama City Beach, about an hour away, and the closest large hospitals are in Panama City.

Crescent Beach

A quiet strip of beach houses and condos south of St. Augustine Beach, between the ocean and the Matanzas River, with one of the widest, calmest beaches on the First Coast. It sits on the Northeast Florida coast, which has had the fewest hurricane direct hits in the state. The catch: almost everything you need is a drive north into St. Augustine.

Navarre Beach

The quiet stretch of the Emerald Coast between Pensacola Beach and Destin, with a long Gulf pier, a sea turtle center and miles of open dunes. It earns our top beach score. The catch: it is a barrier island, and it scores 7.9 out of 10 in our flood risk rankings. The mainland side, Navarre, is cheaper at about $430K and higher up.

Englewood

A laid back Gulf town with a small old downtown and the beaches of Manasota Key, known for shark teeth. At about $375K it is the least expensive town on this list. The catch: it is spread out, and nights out mean a drive to Venice or Sarasota.

Juno Beach

A small, low key oceanfront town with a long fishing pier, a wide beach and sea turtles that nest every summer. Palm Beach International is close, so quiet does not mean remote. The catch: Palm Beach County's average homeowners insurance runs about $6,323 a year, among the highest in the state.

Melbourne Beach

One of the oldest beach towns on the Space Coast, a few quiet streets between the ocean and the Indian River, with rocket launches to watch from the sand. The catch: it is mostly homes, and at about $849K typical, it costs more than the mainland city of Melbourne across the river.

Mexico Beach

A small Gulf town that Hurricane Michael nearly wiped out in 2018 and that has steadily rebuilt around its wide, uncrowded beach. Many homes are new since the storm. The catch: services are still coming back, and it is a reminder that the Panhandle gets the most hurricanes in Florida.

St. George Island

A barrier island with no high rises, a lighthouse in the middle and nine miles of state park beach at the east end. Truly dark nights. The catch: one bridge in and out, and a long drive to a full service hospital or a big airport.

Longboat Key

A quiet island with uncrowded beaches, and St. Armands Circle and Sarasota's theaters a short drive away when you want them. The catch: about $2.1M for a typical home, and it scores 7.5 on our flood list.

Captiva Island

A lush little island next to Sanibel, with some of the best shelling in the country and banyan shaded bike rides to the sunset. The catch: price, about $2.27M for a typical home, and one road in through Sanibel.

How quiet do you want it?

There is a difference between peaceful and isolated. If you want quiet nights but a good dinner within 15 minutes, look at Crescent Beach, Juno Beach or Melbourne Beach. If you want to be truly away, look at Port St. Joe, Mexico Beach and St. George Island, and check how far the nearest hospital is before you fall in love. If money is less of an issue and you want quiet with polish, our list of the best beach towns for quiet luxury goes deeper on that side.

Sources: Florida Coastal town scores and town pages (Nov 2026); US Census Bureau 2020 counts; Florida Office of Economic and Demographic Research 2024 estimate (Melbourne Beach); Florida Coastal flood risk rankings; Florida Office of Insurance Regulation, Property Insurance Stability Report, July 2026.
faq: What is the quietest beach town in Florida?
Port St. Joe on the Forgotten Coast is our top pick: a strong beach score, almost no nightlife and a typical home price around $425K. Crescent Beach and Navarre Beach are close behind.
What is the most affordable quiet beach town in Florida?
Englewood on the Southwest Gulf coast, at about $375K typical, with the beaches of Manasota Key nearby.
Are there quiet beach towns in Florida near a big airport?
Yes. Juno Beach is a short drive from Palm Beach International, and Longboat Key is close to the Sarasota Bradenton airport.
Which quiet Florida beach towns have the lowest flood risk?
Mainland and higher ground towns do best. On the islands on this list, Navarre Beach and Longboat Key score 7.9 and 7.5 out of 10 in our flood rankings, while Mexico Beach scores 4.4.
